about.title: Beaumont Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Beaumont's mix of logistics centers, retail corridors along Beaumont Avenue, and construction tied to the city's growth means workplace injuries here span forklift accidents, falls from scaffolding, and vehicle collisions during work travel. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation regardless of fault, but that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the harm, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside any workers' comp benefits. Beaumont's proximity to I-10 also means delivery drivers and traveling employees face added exposure to third-party vehicle crashes while on the clock. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can look at the details of what happened and explain what options might exist, on a contingency basis so there's no fee unless the case recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why Beaumont Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Angle
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can still be pursued separately. An attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or file a claim. If you're worried about your job because you got hurt, that's worth discussing with an attorney.

items.title: Awareness of Reporting and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to the employer within 30 days, and any separate third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing these windows can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I already filed a workers' comp claim in Beaumont — can I still talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Yes. Workers' comp and a third-party injury claim are separate tracks, and having one doesn't rule out the other. An independent attorney can look at whether someone besides your employer, like a contractor or equipment supplier, contributed to your injury.

items.question: My injury happened while driving for work near I-10 or Beaumont Avenue — does that count as a workplace injury?
items.answer: Often yes, if you were performing job duties at the time. These cases can involve both a workers' comp claim and a potential third-party claim against another driver, which is why it's worth having an attorney review the specifics.

items.question: What if my employer told me not to report my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation or discouraging you from reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. You generally have 30 days to report the injury to your employer, so it's important to act promptly and consider speaking with an attorney if you feel pressured.
